reasons: Both answers flag the Montana WDEA good-cause issue, say that the work location decides which law applies, adapt the plan with release, PIP and counsel options, and include disclaimers. B goes further on the good-cause problem, with a dedicated evidence file (reviews that cut against the company, a decision memo), a correct explanation of the grievance-procedure exhaustion effect, and a Montana registration check. A mischaracterizes the grievance-copy step as a requirement, and it dates the job-performance ground to the 2021 amendments. B misdates the amendments to 2019, so on errors the two are roughly even.

A: Says the 2021 amendments added failure to perform job duties to good cause; that ground was in the original WDEA definition
Says the WDEA requires giving a copy of the internal grievance procedure within 7 days; it is a condition for requiring exhaustion, not a mandate
B: Says the WDEA amendments on good cause and the grievance procedure were made in 2019; the major amendments were in 2021
